verdict: Avoid new steel re-rolling/TMT exposure in Jammu until local demand signals turn; lend only to branded, integrated re-rollers with verified order books and tight monthly controls.
title: Jammu steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A re-rolling mill buys billets or scrap, heats and rolls them into TMT bars, and sells into construction demand — government works, municipal contracts, private builders. **Cash is made on the spread between input cost and per-tonne realisation, not on volume alone.** Margins are thin and swing with scrap and billet prices; rating reports flag that sudden price fluctuations can hit margins [10]. Working capital sits in inventory and receivables, and peers carry moderately high working-capital needs supported by bank lines [11]. So when a proposal lands, check the conversion spread and receivable days first; if the buyer mix is mostly government contractors, ask for the payment history on those bills.

## What has changed in Jammu now
**The local demand engine has stalled.** Jammu and Kashmir GST collections are down 10.6% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], and electricity demand is -0.5% against India's +9.5% [D] — both local stress signals. On top of that, development works are stalled amid a contractors-government standoff [2], and JMC contractors are protesting anti-contractor policies, payment delays and revised EMD norms [3]. **TMT demand in this city runs through exactly those stalled public works.** Nationally the picture is steadier — IIP for NIC 24 output is +2.4% YoY [D] — but that does not reach Jammu's site-level demand. Note the local sources are from July 2026 and the data pack runs to Sep-2026; treat them as recent but confirm current status with the customer.

## Where the growth is — and who to avoid
**Pursue branded TMT re-rollers with a dealer network and private-builder sales, not pure government-order mills.** Peer results show the branded, integrated model working: Steel Exchange India clocked ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [6], and Rathi Steel posted over ₹200 crore with ~28.86% volume growth [7]. Branding commands a premium — Captain Steel's brand ambassador spend helped it price above market [9]. **Avoid mills whose order book is dominated by JMC or state public works** until the contractor standoff clears [2][3]; their receivables will stretch. Also avoid thinly capitalised standalone re-rollers with no scrap sourcing tie-up — collect from customer on scrap sourcing and billet contracts.

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the asset.** Keep tenor short, match limits to the inventory-plus-receivable cycle, and take monthly stock and book-debt statements. Rating reports show gearing can move fast — Kubair's gearing deteriorated to 1.80x from 1.40x in one year on debt-funded acquisition and higher working-capital borrowings [10]. So when a proposal lands, check gearing trend over two years; if it has risen more than the peer range, ask for the debt-funded capex plan and repayment source. Take monthly: stock statement, sales register, top-five debtor ageing, and electricity consumption as a proxy for running hours.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local demand and payment chain, not just the borrower's books.** If JMC/state payment delays persist [3], contractor receivables will age — trigger a limit review. If GST collections in J&K stay negative [D], site demand is not recovering. If the borrower's electricity consumption falls while sales stay flat, suspect stock build-up. If scrap or billet prices swing sharply, margins compress [10] — ask for the pass-through clause in sales contracts. Collect from customer on any figure not in this note.

Two more negative prints [D] -> pause new sanctions in the cluster
Standoff continues past Q3 [2][3] -> review all government-order-dependent exposures
Consumption falls while sales flat -> suspect stock build-up, seek physical verification
Sharp swing with no pass-through clause [10] -> reprice or reduce exposure
